title: Dar por: Taking Something as Settled

sections.content:
*Dar por* + participle (or adjective) means to treat something as finished, lost or certain, whether or not it really is: *Dieron por perdida la cosecha* ("They gave up the harvest for lost"). It is a judgement that someone makes. You have met *dar por hecho* as a phrase in B2 Unit 5; here you see how the whole pattern is built.

The participle agrees with the thing that follows, in gender and number, just as it does after *estar* (B2 Unit 20): *dio por terminado el caso*, *dio por terminadas las pruebas*. With *que* the participle does not change: *Doy por hecho que vendrá*.

sections.title: dar por + participle
rows: El juez dio por terminado el caso.
The judge declared the case closed.
They gave the cows up for lost.
Doy por hecho que vendrá mañana.
I take it for granted that he will come tomorrow.
He took it for granted that we would win.

sections.content: *Dar por* is not the same as *estar*. *Está perdida* says the cows are lost; *Las dieron por perdidas* says people decided they were lost, and they may have been wrong: *Lo dieron por muerto, pero estaba vivo*.
